_comment: The fleet agent's own allowlist, matching docs/examples/fleet.conf.
This file is the trust boundary. The router names an identifier; the agent
looks it up here and runs what *this* file says. Nothing the router sends
is ever interpolated into a command line, so a fully compromised router can
reorder these rows and cannot add one.
Keep it in step with the router's configuration. The two sides compute a
digest independently over the identifiers, placement, and architectures
below; when they disagree the router issues no mutating verb and every
orchestrated target becomes ineligible. That is fleet-wide, not per-host:
a host removed from one file and not the other stops orchestration for the
ones that are still in both. Compare them before enabling:
